notes: PSA 13 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.18. Prostate volume 72 mL. csPCa 0.78.

note_sections.t: Assessment of rising PSA values to 13.0 ng/mL in the setting of previously confirmed prostate malignancy.

A 71-year-old retired plumber entered initial evaluation in late 2023 when routine laboratory screening indicated a PSA level of 7.8 ng/mL. Chronic hypercholesterolaemia and knee osteoarthritis characterize his medical background, managed with atorvastatin, simvastatin, and tamsulosin. Early 2024 transperineal sampling confirmed adenocarcinoma classified as ISUP GG 3, placing him under ongoing surveillance. He is married and lives with his partner, maintains a regular gardening routine, and abstains from alcohol. A non-smoker, his overall clinical status remains steady; an autumn 2024 cardiology assessment verified controlled cardiovascular parameters, and he maintains biannual dental visits. He denies bone discomfort, haematuria, or unexplained weight reduction, while urinary complaints stay minimal despite the documented benign prostatic hyperplasia.

DRE — texture: smooth and firm; mobility: unremarkable; asymmetry: none. Normal DRE. The gland presents as symmetrically enlarged without discrete nodules. Vital parameters remain stable, recording a blood pressure of 119/81 mmHg and a regular pulse of 63 bpm. Systemic assessment reveals no palpable lymphadenopathy or abdominal masses.
